description: Phase-WIKI-A — graph analytics layer on top of the existing wiki GraphIndex. 3 cheap-win stories adapted from the graphify analysis (memory: reference-graphify-wiki-improvements-2026-05-19). Aura already has internal/wiki/graph_index.go with Degree, OutNeighbors, InNeighbors, Neighbors(slug, depth) — the substrate is right, the analytics layer is what's missing. A01 (god-nodes) + A02 (path-finding) are pure additions over the existing index. A03 (confidence labels on related:) touches the Page schema with backward-compat YAML unmarshaler — bigger blast radius, last in queue on purpose. Reference doc D:/tmp/graphify cloned 2026-05-19. Master HEAD at queue creation: d104e6ed. STRICT one-story-exit per Ralph CLAUDE.md.

userStories.title: God-node ranking via degree centrality + tool + API + dashboard widget
userStories.description: Surface the most-connected wiki pages as 'god nodes' so the LLM and the operator can bootstrap on the project's hubs. Use degree-centrality (in+out edges) for v0 — PageRank is a follow-up. Aura's GraphIndex (internal/wiki/graph_index.go) already exposes Degree(slug)(in,out) per node + NodeCount + Meta — the new code walks all nodes and sorts. (a) internal/wiki/godnodes.go (NEW, ~80 LOC): new type `GodNode struct { Slug, Title, Category string; InDegree, OutDegree, TotalDegree int }`. New method `func (g *GraphIndex) TopByDegree(topK int) []GodNode` that walks g.meta (under RLock), computes in+out degree per slug via g.Degree, sorts desc by TotalDegree (ties broken alphabetically for determinism), returns the top K. Edge case: topK<=0 returns empty slice; topK > NodeCount returns all nodes. (b) New Go tool in internal/agent/tools/registry/: file `wiki_godnodes.go` exposing a Tool with Name="recall_god_nodes" + Description explaining when to use it (e.g. 'List the most-connected wiki pages — useful as a project overview when starting a conversation or summarizing what Aura knows about'). Parameters: `top_k int` (default 10, min 1, max 50). Execute calls into the wiki Store / GraphIndex. (c) New HTTP endpoint in internal/api/wiki.go (or a sibling file): `GET /api/wiki/godnodes?top_k=N` returning `{"nodes": [{slug, title, category, in, out, total}]}`. Reuse the existing auth pattern (bearer token via internal/api/router.go). (d) Frontend widget in web/src/components/WikiPanel.tsx (or sibling): a small 'Top hubs' card showing the top-10 list with click-through links to each wiki page. Use the existing api.ts client + Trans helper for i18n. (e) Tests: internal/wiki/godnodes_test.go with a fixture GraphIndex populated via LoadFromPages (4-6 pages with deterministic edges) + assert TopByDegree(3) returns expected slugs in expected order. Tool test covers default top_k + bounds clamping. API test exercises the HTTP path via httptest.

userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: read internal/wiki/graph_index.go in FULL (it's ~300 lines and the mental model is critical — note the RWMutex, the upsertLocked invariants, the In/Out/Neighbors signatures, the Degree() helper). Also read internal/wiki/store.go to understand how the Store wires GraphIndex into the rest of the system (the Store owns the GraphIndex; tools/api need a handle to either the Store or the index). Also read 1-2 existing tools in internal/agent/tools/registry/ (search_memory.go is a good template — same shape: Name/Description/Parameters/Execute). Also read internal/api/wiki.go to see how existing /api/wiki/* endpoints are wired + the auth pattern. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: degree-centrality only, NO PageRank in this story (PageRank is a future follow-up — it needs power-iteration over the graph and isn't necessary for v0). NO Leiden clustering. NO caching layer (TopByDegree walks N nodes which is <1ms for 46-50 nodes; cache is premature). The widget is read-only — no actions, no edit, just display + click-through. INVARIANT: the GraphIndex API stays read-only externally (TopByDegree is a query, no mutation). DASHBOARD STYLE: match the existing WikiGraphView.tsx aesthetic — don't introduce new colors or icons; reuse lucide-react icons already imported elsewhere (e.g. Network, Activity, Sparkles).

userStories.title: wiki_path tool — shortest-path BFS between two slugs
userStories.description: Add a path-finding capability: given two slugs, return the shortest chain of [[wiki-link]] / related: edges connecting them (or nil if no path within max_hops). Lets the LLM answer 'how is X connected to Y?' with the actual chain instead of guessing. (a) internal/wiki/graph_index.go: new method `func (g *GraphIndex) ShortestPath(from, to string, maxHops int) []string` returning the slug chain (inclusive of both endpoints) or nil if no path exists / from==to / maxHops<=0 / from not in index. Implementation: BFS from `from`, track parent map, reconstruct path when `to` is reached. Use the existing in+out edge expansion (same logic as Neighbors — paths can traverse either direction). (b) New tool in internal/agent/tools/registry/wiki_path.go with Name="wiki_path", parameters: `from_slug string` (required), `to_slug string` (required), `max_hops int` (default 5, min 1, max 20). Execute returns the path as a list + a human-readable narration ('X → Y → Z connects them via 2 hops through topic-Y'). If no path: returns explicit 'no path within N hops' (NOT an error — absence is a valid result). (c) HTTP endpoint GET /api/wiki/path?from=X&to=Y&max_hops=N → `{"path": [...], "hops": int}` or `{"path": null, "reason": "no path within N hops"}`. Same auth as /api/wiki/godnodes. (d) Tests: graph_index_test.go gains TestShortestPath covering: same node (returns [slug]), direct neighbor (2 nodes), 3-hop chain, no-path case, max_hops cap respected (path exists at hop=4, max_hops=3 returns nil), unknown from/to slug. Tool test exercises happy path + no-path narration. API test asserts both JSON shapes.

Single atomic commit prefix: feat(wiki): wiki_path tool + /api/wiki/path BFS shortest-path (US-WIKI-A02)
userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: read internal/wiki/graph_index.go Neighbors() (lines ~181-221) — it already does BFS with frontier expansion; ShortestPath shares the structure but adds parent tracking + early termination on hitting `to`. Standard textbook BFS — use map[string]string parent + queue ([]string or []struct{slug string; depth int}). HOLD RLock for the entire BFS (single read transaction). Path reconstruction: walk parent map backwards from `to` to `from`, reverse the slice. NO PRIORITY QUEUE — unweighted graph, BFS suffices. DO NOT change Neighbors() or the existing methods. DO NOT introduce a 'depth' field on NodeMeta. The narration string for the tool result is for the LLM consumer — keep it short and factual ('slug-a -> slug-b -> slug-c (2 hops)'), no emoji, no markdown. NO frontend widget in this story — A01 owns the visual surface; this is tool + API only (the LLM uses it via tool calls). If the user wants a 'Show path between two pages' panel, that's a follow-up. PROBE COVERAGE: optional — add a probe_chat case (cmd/probe_chat/cases.go) that uses wiki_path against a known-stable pair in the live wiki only if the case can be made non-flaky; otherwise document the deferral in the commit message.

userStories.title: Confidence labels on related: frontmatter (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS)
userStories.description: Extend Page.Related from []string to []RelatedRef{Slug, Confidence} with backward-compatible YAML parsing — bare strings auto-promote to EXTRACTED, explicit dicts carry their confidence. Retrievers downweight INFERRED edges; AMBIGUOUS edges are excluded from default retrieval but surface in a review queue. (a) internal/wiki/schema.go: new type `RelatedRef struct { Slug string \`yaml:"slug"\`; Confidence string \`yaml:"confidence,omitempty"\` }`. Custom UnmarshalYAML on RelatedRef accepting both shapes: scalar string (slug-only) -> RelatedRef{Slug:s, Confidence:"EXTRACTED"}; mapping -> standard unmarshal with default Confidence="EXTRACTED" if absent. Validation in Validate(): Confidence must be one of EXTRACTED|INFERRED|AMBIGUOUS|"" (empty defaults to EXTRACTED). (b) Change Page.Related from []string to []RelatedRef. Bump CurrentSchemaVersion from 2 to 3 — old schema_version=2 pages still parse via the backward-compat unmarshaler (bare strings work forever; the version bump is the marker for new writes that emit explicit confidence). (c) Update all call sites that read page.Related — grep for `.Related` across internal/ and adapt. internal/wiki/graph_index.go upsertLocked() builds edges from page.Related — switch to reading .Slug. (d) Retrieval rerank: in internal/storage/search/ wherever the graph index is consulted for ranking (grep for 'GraphIndex' + 'Degree' + 'Neighbors'), apply a confidence-aware penalty: EXTRACTED = base weight 1.0; INFERRED = 0.6; AMBIGUOUS = 0.0 (excluded). Add an opt-in flag for callers that want to surface AMBIGUOUS (e.g. the review queue). (e) Tests: schema_test.go extended with TestRelatedRef_BareStringParsesAsExtracted, TestRelatedRef_ExplicitConfidence, TestRelatedRef_InvalidConfidenceFails, TestPage_SchemaV2_LegacyRelatedStillParses, TestPage_SchemaV3_RoundTrip. graph_index_test.go updated to construct pages with RelatedRef (backward compat for tests still using bare strings via a small helper). (f) The LLM writer prompt (internal/agent/promptplan or wherever the system prompt for wiki writes is defined) is unchanged for now — the LLM keeps emitting bare strings, and they auto-promote to EXTRACTED. A follow-up story can teach the LLM to emit INFERRED when it's guessing.

userStories.notes: BIGGEST BLAST RADIUS OF THE THREE — touches Page schema + every reader of page.Related. Run AFTER A01 + A02 land so any conflict shows up against a clean base. GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: (1) read internal/wiki/schema.go in FULL; (2) `grep -rn '\.Related' internal/` to enumerate every call site; (3) read internal/wiki/parser.go for the existing frontmatter parse path; (4) read internal/wiki/graph_index.go upsertLocked (~line 120) — that's the in-graph consumer. CRITICAL INVARIANT: existing wiki pages on disk must read without rewrite. The custom UnmarshalYAML is what makes this possible — implement it carefully + test it FIRST before changing the field type. ANTIPATTERN GUARD: do NOT migrate existing pages on disk (no batch rewrite, no schema_version bump on legacy pages). They keep their schema_version=2 + bare-string related: list forever; only NEW writes by the LLM emit schema_version=3. DO NOT change the LLM prompt in this story — the prompt change is a follow-up (it needs eval + measurement of false-positive INFERRED labels). DO NOT add a dashboard panel for the AMBIGUOUS review queue in this story — surface it in the existing wiki_issues / proposed_updates table queue (compose env already mentions them) as a row with kind=ambiguous_related. The retrieval rerank in (d) is the load-bearing user-visible change: with INFERRED downweighted to 0.6 and AMBIGUOUS excluded, the search_memory tool will return slightly different rankings post-deploy. Verify on a known-stable probe case that the new ranking doesn't break a previously-PASSing case (run cmd/probe_chat suite if available, or document the deferral). YAML PARSING: gopkg.in/yaml.v3 supports custom Unmarshaler — the signature is `(n *yaml.Node) error`. Switch on n.Kind: yaml.ScalarNode = bare string path; yaml.MappingNode = decode into a struct alias to avoid infinite recursion. Search the codebase for existing custom UnmarshalYAML implementations as templates.
